named_partner_consumed.applied_result: Uniform restriction to an autonomous subset; a cardinality-minimal POS3 counterexample has no proper autonomous nonchain. This removes the zero-distinguisher blocker-sibling branch under the full uniform extension law.

new_result.name: opposite-sign two-distinguisher balance theorem
new_result.statement: For any finite poset and incomparable a,b with exactly two distinguishers, if the two asymmetric comparabilities have opposite signs relative to a<b, then 1/3 <= Pr(a<b) <= 2/3.
new_result.method: Delete a,b and the two distinguishers; for each exact skeleton retain all insertion-gap multiplicities. A right-shift/left-shift adjacent-word injection proves the 1:2 ratio bound separately in every fiber.
new_result.minimal_counterexample_consequence: For an extreme orientation Pr(a<b)>2/3 with exactly two distinguishers, both distinguishers must have the same positive sign. At the inherited clean first-fork sibling pair, the exactly-two branch is therefore a coherent delayed positive second fork; otherwise there are at least three delayed distinguishers.

adversarial_boundary.meaning: Two same-sign distinguishers can be extreme; the opposite-sign hypothesis is essential.

verification.coverage: 1780 interval instances in each canonical case; all 357 naturally labelled five-point closures, 1984 incomparable pairs, 214 exactly-two opposite-sign pairs.

next_obligation: Propagate either the >=3 delayed-distinguisher branch or the coherent exactly-two positive second-fork branch to the next strong-majority boundary, using exact channel mass and width-three/autonomy constraints, to force balance, a 4-antichain, or a proper autonomous nonchain.
